title: Atomberg Technologies Files for IPO With ₹450 Crore Fresh Issue as Early Investors Head for Exit
excerpt: The IIT-Bombay-founded smart appliance maker plans to list on Indian exchanges, with early backers including A91 Partners and Jungle Ventures selling shares through a 7.65 crore OFS.
body:
• Atomberg Technologies has filed its DRHP with SEBI for an IPO comprising a ₹450 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of 7.65 crore shares by existing investors.
  • Revenue from operations rose 34.8% to ₹1,293.77 crore in FY26, though the company remains loss-making with a restated loss of ₹148.88 crore.
  • The company claims 46% market share in India's premium fan segment and operates through nearly 47,000 retail touchpoints across 1,600 cities.
  • IPO proceeds will fund debt repayment (₹90 crore), brand marketing (₹150 crore), and R&D (₹100 crore).

IPO Structure and Investor Exits

Mumbai-based consumer appliance maker Atomberg Technologies has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India to raise funds through an initial public offering. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to ₹450 crore and an offer for sale of 76.54 million shares from existing investors, according to the filing dated August 21.

A91 Emerging Fund I LLP, V-Sciences Investments, Jungle Ventures IV, and Inflexor Opportunities Fund 1 are among the shareholders selling through the OFS, marking exits or partial stake reductions for some of Atomberg's earliest backers. The company has raised approximately $126.5 million in funding to date from investors including Steadview Capital and Temasek Holdings, which co-led an $86 million Series C round that valued the company at $425-450 million.

Atomberg also plans to raise up to ₹90 crore through a pre-IPO placement before filing its Red Herring Prospectus. If completed, the fresh issue size will be reduced by the amount raised in the placement. ICICI Securities, Avendus Capital, and IIFL Capital Services have been appointed as bankers to the issue.

Revenue Growing, Losses Narrowing

Atomberg's revenue from operations rose 34.8% to ₹1,293.77 crore in FY26 from ₹959.51 crore in FY25, according to the DRHP. However, adjusted EBITDA declined to ₹37.12 crore from ₹51.35 crore during the same period, reflecting heavier spending on brand building and category expansion. The restated net loss narrowed to ₹148.88 crore in FY26 from ₹199.08 crore in FY24.

Online channels contributed ₹456.45 crore to FY26 revenue, nearly doubling from ₹234.51 crore in FY24. Offline revenue rose to ₹820.11 crore from ₹562.47 crore over the same period, with Tier 2 and smaller cities accounting for 49.57% of offline sales.

Premium Fan Leader Expanding Into New Categories

Founded in 2012 by IIT-Bombay alumni Manoj Meena and Sibabrata Das, Atomberg started as a maker of energy-efficient BLDC (brushless direct current) fans before expanding into mixer grinders, water purifiers, cold-pressed juicers, and smart locks. The company also manufactures proprietary motors and electronic controllers for enterprise customers including Voltas, Godrej, and Blue Star through its subsidiary Atomberg Innovations.

According to market research firm Redseer, Atomberg held a 46.08% share by cumulative sales value in India's premium fan segment — defined as fans with an average selling price above ₹3,500 — in FY26. India's consumer appliances market is estimated at $4.69 billion in FY26, with the premium segment growing as rising incomes and urbanisation drive demand for energy-efficient products.

R&D-Heavy Model, Expanding Distribution

The company spent ₹86.79 crore on R&D in FY26, or 6.71% of revenue, and employed 254 engineers — 25.32% of its permanent workforce. It operates two leased manufacturing facilities in Pune and distributes through 626 distributors and direct dealers, reaching nearly 47,000 retail touchpoints across more than 18,000 pin codes.

Atomberg plans to use IPO proceeds to repay ₹90 crore in borrowings, spend ₹150 crore on brand awareness and performance marketing, and allocate ₹100 crore to R&D as it expands into adjacent categories including water purification and motorised food preparation.

What to Watch

The listing will test investor appetite for a loss-making consumer brand in a market that has increasingly rewarded profitable growth. Atomberg's premium positioning and rapid revenue growth are clear strengths, but the widening gap between revenue and profitability — adjusted EBITDA fell even as revenue grew — will draw scrutiny from public market investors accustomed to margin discipline.
